events.title: Hungary's First King Is Canonized
events.description: King Stephen I, who founded the Christian Kingdom of Hungary, was canonized along with his son, Prince Emeric. Stephen's feast day is now celebrated as Hungary's national day.
events.significance: Hungary still marks August 20 as its national day, honoring Stephen as the founder of the Hungarian state.

events.title: Wang Yangming Crushes the Prince of Ning's Rebellion
events.description: On the third day of fighting, the philosopher-general Wang Yangming defeated the rebel Zhu Chenhao. This ended a rebellion against the Ming dynasty's Zhengde Emperor.
events.significance: The victory kept the Ming throne secure. It also showed that one of China's leading thinkers could succeed as a military commander.

events.title: The De Witt Brothers Are Lynched in The Hague
events.description: Johan de Witt, the former Grand Pensionary of Holland, and his brother Cornelis were killed by a mob in The Hague during the Dutch Republic's 'Disaster Year'.
events.significance: The killings ended the leadership of a statesman who had guided the Dutch Republic for decades. They paved the way for the rise of William III of Orange.

events.title: Leon Trotsky Is Attacked in Mexico
events.description: In Mexico City, the Soviet agent Ramón Mercader struck the exiled revolutionary Leon Trotsky on the head with an ice axe. Trotsky died of his wounds the next day.
events.significance: The attack removed Joseph Stalin's most prominent exiled rival. It remains one of the best-known political assassinations of the 20th century.

events.title: NASA Launches Voyager 2
events.description: Voyager 2 lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, aboard a Titan/Centaur rocket. It was launched a few weeks before its twin, Voyager 1.
events.significance: Voyager 2 went on to become the only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune. It gave humanity its first close-up views of those distant worlds.
